objectives.description: Terminal-write genuine pending: a terminal write is genuinely pending at a sample (SenderWritableAtSample=false, PeerUnreadAtSample>0, stage 'kernel-write-pending'), then interrupted by a total deadline. Native Linux.
Terminal-write genuine pending interrupted by peer listener cancellation. Native Linux.
Close_notify genuine pending (live shutdown observed pending) using a zero-window peer, interrupted by a phase deadline. Native Linux.
Close_notify genuine pending using a zero-window peer and a gated TLS proxy, interrupted by peer listener cancellation. Native Linux.
Encrypted byte-cap enforcement: declared encrypted cap enforced on the drain; independent tamper control NC-1.
Plaintext byte-cap enforcement: declared plaintext cap enforced; observed encrypted wire bytes bounded by the encrypted cap.
Cleanup/accounting: socket Closed, Active=0, accepted=completed+failed, permits balanced, no unobserved exceptions, attempt lifetime bounded.
Independently observed peer application receipt: the peer application reads the terminal message and the runner validates a receipt journal record (digest + byte count) against the campaign journal.
Negative controls NC-1 (ciphertext-cap tamper) and NC-2 (deadline-renewal tamper) are detected; control-failure outcomes recorded with bounded attempts.
Repeatability: per-cell discovery bounds (<=4), two qualifying repeats on a qualified cell, seeded determinism, repeat-classification equality.
Distinguish the four guarantee levels: local write completion, TLS close_notify transmission, peer receipt, verified peer receipt.

job_time.note: hard cap: timeout-minutes 45 on the job; the campaign driver step is bounded with coreutils timeout 2700 s; per-attempt watchdog 3500 ms

resources.concurrency: max-parallel: 1; cells serialized; one job per campaign
resources.network: ephemeral IPv4 loopback only; no external endpoints
resources.disk: results/ only (journals and transcripts); bounded upload of results/

nc1_ciphertext_cap_tamper.oracle: mutate the declared encrypted cap (32768 -> 131072) before the drain; the campaign must detect the mismatch: outcome 'cap-checks-failed', observed WireBytes > declared cap; the cell stops as non-qualifying (positive control of the cap oracle).

nc2_deadline_renewal.oracle: extend the total deadline beyond the bounded total_elapsed_bound_ms; the campaign must detect: outcome 'induced-but-checks-failed' with total elapsed > bound.

notes: Negative-control runs record control-failure observations; they are not defects and do not qualify the campaign.
NC-1/NC-2 attempts are bounded by the campaign budgets.

repeatability.rule: one or more qualifying discovery runs plus two qualifying repeats on the same profile ordinal; stop the cell after a qualifying result; repeat classification must equal the discovery classification (predeclared rule, mirroring Q-B5B-09-TLS-E1: 'qualified is the cell-level repeatability result of three oracle-passing runs with the same profile').
repeatability.determinism: per-cell seeds (L1..L7): 1001..1007; the same seed replays the ordered discovery profiles; repeat runs reuse the selected profile ordinal.
repeatability.attempt_bound: bounded by budgets.attempts (lifetime 3500 ms; discovery <= 4; cap cells <= 3)

mechanisms.fixed_link: ephemeral IPv4 loopback TLS listener; the peer parks its receive direction after the pipelined terminal write; no relay, no delayed encrypted-write await, no privileged network change, no external endpoint (adapted from Q-B5B-09-TLS-E1 fixed_link for native Linux).
mechanisms.zero_window_peer: the peer is a separate process running python3 stdlib ssl server; it sets SO_RCVBUF to the minimum allowed and stops reading after the handshake; the kernel advertises a zero TCP receive window, so the client send queue backs up and the terminal write (or the close_notify write) stays pending.

deep_queue_profiles.note: deep queue required for native-Linux close_notify induction; recorded as a non-qualifying observation where the pending stage is not induced

mechanisms.gated_tls_proxy: a python3 ssl-based TCP proxy between the campaign sender and the peer; the proxy observes the close_notify record on the sender side and holds (gates) forwarding for a bounded gate interval; the proxy journal records the gate decision and the TLS identity (protocol version, cipher).

interruption.total_deadline: absolute monotonic deadline interrupts the pending write or pending shutdown via owner cancellation (L1, L3). Terminal-write pending bound 310 ms; close_notify pending bound 120 ms; total elapsed bound 500 ms.
interruption.phase_deadline: close_notify cells use a phase deadline bounding the shutdown to <= 120 ms (L3).
interruption.listener_cancellation: the peer stops its listener after a bounded interval (L2, L4); the pending write or shutdown is cancelled through the linked cancellation, mirroring Q-B5B-09-TLS-E1 P4-deep-listener-stop.

genuine_pending_confirmation: Confirmed == true (a genuinely pending write was observed)
SenderWritableAtSample == false (the write had not completed at the sample)
the attempt journal contains the 'kernel-write-pending' stage
close_notify cells: the live shutdown was observed pending (a close_notify write, not only the pre-terminal write)

guarantee_levels.local_write_completion: WriteAsync/FlushAsync returned after TLS encryption and kernel acceptance (journaled as WriteCompleted/FlushCompleted; observed in the journals of the smaller production-like cases). This is the ladder's base and is NOT close_notify transmission.
guarantee_levels.tls_close_notify_transmission: the close alert is delivered to the TLS layer and transmitted; native-Linux cells L3/L4 establish it via the live-pending observation (a close_notify write observed pending and bounded) — transmission after interruption or gate release. Not established for production HEAD; candidate-only evidence.
guarantee_levels.peer_receipt: the peer observes EOF or reads the terminal message (journal: PeerRead, PeerUnread, clean TLS EOF).
guarantee_levels.verified_peer_receipt: the peer application confirms reading the terminal message; the peer records a receipt (message bytes + digest + receipt_ms) to the peer journal; the runner validates the receipt against the campaign journal (digest + byte count); at least one valid receipt is required for the peer-receipt cell L7; distinct from local write completion and transport completion.

peer_receipt_oracle.design: independent observation: the peer application runs as a separate process (python3 stdlib ssl server) and writes receipts to the peer journal; the campaign runner validates receipts against the campaign journal.

receipt_record.validation: the runner requires at least one valid receipt per L7 run; receipt.sha256 must equal the campaign journal terminal message digest and receipt.message_bytes must equal the expected terminal byte count; a receipt without a matching campaign digest is a journal inconsistency, not a qualification.

cross_checks: PeerUnreadAtEnd == 0 for the cooperative cell; the receipt is recorded by the peer before it records EOF.
